newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA LIFTS LIMITS ON FOREIGN PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA LIFTS LIMITS ON FOREIGN PLAYERS.

text.p: Russia's soccer authorities lifted restrictions on foreigners playing in its premier league on Wednesday to bring it into line with the rest of Europe, a league official said.

Leonid Lipovoi, vice-president of the Professional Football League, said a rule barring clubs from fielding more than three foreigners had been scrapped in accordance with the Bosman decision lifting such restrictions elsewhere on the continent.
"We decided to cancel all limitations for foreign players in the premier league to keep to European rules and to be able to march together down the Bosman path" Lipovoi told Reuters.
"The whole of Europe including Russia has to follow the same rules and we welcome this."
He said the Professional Football League hoped to attract more foreign players in the 1997 season starting next month.
Russian teams have many players from former Soviet republics but have not had the money to attract top players from Western clubs.
Limits will remain in place in Russia's other leagues. Teams in the first division will be allowed to field five foreign players, and second and third division teams will be limited to three.
